answer: Neighborhood depth gate. Each identity must hold links to peers that themselves link outward, and routing weight scales with two-hop reach. A dense cluster of fresh identities forms a shallow island that cannot route because its neighbors share the same thin boundary. Spawning convincing depth costs the attacker a tide of new links per fake, since every extra hop multiplies the required distinct counterparties. The added pigment here is a verifiable outward-degree count, so forging depth means paying for real connectivity, not just registrations.
